title: JSON-RPC
subtitle: JSON-RPC is the transport under the Model Context Protocol surfaces I build and consume.

stats.label: custom error codes a client can branch on
MCP servers mapped by the read-only explorer

lede: In FAFO Core and Function Forge I expected the number of tools to grow faster than anyone could hand-wire gateway routes. So I made JSON-RPC 2.0, the envelope of the Model Context Protocol, something the gateway serves from generated code. The gateway is an Axum server that speaks MCP over HTTP with the .well-known MCP configuration, protected-resource metadata and session headers. At build time a generator turns a YAML trio per tool into handlers and routing, so a new function becomes callable without anyone editing gateway code, and the gateway and its catalog cannot drift apart. Function Forge is itself an MCP tool on this envelope.
quote: I treat the wire envelope as plumbing that should be generated, typed and boring.
evidence: MCP server design: JSON-RPC routing generated from YAML at build time, with 22 custom error codes a client can branch on.
Resilient transports: a streaming session that broke on container restarts replaced by stateless JSON-RPC over HTTPS.
Agent-to-agent messaging: JSON-RPC envelopes aligned with the Agent Client Protocol over Redis streams, including a call that starts an agent on another host.
author: Corey James
